claim: The new wrapper drops every analyzer diagnostic whose location is not in source, including Location.None. `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` uses `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax`, so a source-declared positional record property (its declaring syntax is a ParameterSyntax) gets a null location. Example: `[MessagePackObject] public record R([property: Key(null)] string A);` in the compiling assembly. That property's BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull error is now silently dropped by `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation`, even though the offending symbol is in this compilation. The same applies to any other diagnostic created with a null location for a source symbol: it is now dropped where it was reported before.

claim: The reportDiagnostic wrapper now silently drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the current compilation. This includes diagnostics with Location.None, which the old code could report (e.g. FirstOrDefault()?.GetLocation() returning null yields Location.None). It also covers any diagnostics with source locations from other compilations. Users may stop seeing MsgPack00x diagnostics that were previously reported, e.g. on global/project-level diagnostics.

claim: The change raises MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth from 500 to 5000. This is a tenfold loosening of the recursion/depth limit that protects against stack overflow when deserializing untrusted data. It is unrelated to the requirement, which concerns a generator/analyzer crash. A deeply nested payload now gets through up to 5000 nested levels, and the default stack may be exhausted before the limit trips. That is an uncatchable StackOverflow crash (DoS).

claim: The reportDiagnostic wrapper silently drops any diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the compilation. Several diagnostics are created with a null location, e.g. MemberNeedsKey, and for the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic, GetPropertyIdentifierLocation can now return null. A null location is Location.None, which is not in source. These diagnostics are discarded even for source types where the identifier cast fails, for example when the member is a field or the syntax is not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax. This can suppress user-protective diagnostics, such as MsgPack004 or the AOT key diagnostics, for source-declared members.
